title: Bijectivity of the canonical open-object cohomology map
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $F$ an abelian sheaf on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], $q\in\mathbb N$, and $U\subseteq X$ open [def-weil-open-immersion]. The explicitly constructed map $m_U:\operatorname{Ext}^q(A_U,F)\to H^q(U_{et},j_U^*F)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-open-object-cohomology-map] is bijective. No compatibility between different opens is asserted.

source.place: Lemma cohomology-of-open, proof by restriction of an injective resolution; free-representable/Yoneda and constant-sheaf adjunctions. Explicit identity-generator construction and unit compatibility supplied by F2.

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution I of F. Restriction is exact and preserves injectives since its extension-by-zero left adjoint is exact. Identify inverse image with localization restriction, so the pulled-back resolution computes cohomology on U. Use the Ext/injective-resolution comparison on both sites.

The sheafification/free/Yoneda adjunction identifies Hom(A_U,I) with I(U) in each degree. The constant-sheaf adjunction identifies Hom(Z_U,j_U^*I) with the same sections. The composite is exactly pullback followed by precomposition with the constructed identity-generator map k_U. These additive bijections commute with the differentials and therefore induce a bijection on cohomology. This covers q=0 and the empty open as well.
